module_title: Real-World Case Studies 4: Storage, Search & Cloud
description: End-to-end interview blueprints: Design Google Drive / Dropbox (File Chunking, Deduplication & Sync Protocol), TinyURL / Bitly URL Shortener, and Google Web Crawler with PageRank.

topics.title: Case Study: Design Google Drive / Dropbox (Chunking, Content Hashing & Sync)
topics.definition: Design a cloud file storage and synchronization service supporting 500 million users, cross-device multi-folder synchronization, delta sync (syncing only modified bytes), and content deduplication.
topics.why_we_need_it: Uploading a 2GB file after editing 1 sentence should NOT re-upload 2GB of data. Delta chunking and content hashing are premier system design concepts.
topics.real_world_analogy: A puzzle box: instead of mailing an entire giant wooden puzzle when you change 1 piece, you only mail the 1 modified puzzle piece. The recipient puts the piece into their existing puzzle frame.
topics.how_it_works:
1. Client-Side Chunking: Files are split into 4MB chunks using rolling hash algorithms (e.g. Rabin Fingerprinting or CDC).
2. Content-Addressed Storage: Each chunk is hashed with SHA-256 (`Chunk_Hash = SHA256(data)`). Chunks are named by their hash and stored in S3.
3. Global Deduplication: If 1,000 users upload the same 100MB PDF, S3 stores the chunks ONCE; metadata tables simply map 1,000 user file records to the same underlying chunk hashes.
4. Delta Sync: When a file is edited, the client re-hashes chunks, detects only Chunk #4 has changed, and uploads only the 4MB of Chunk #4.
5. Notification & Sync Service: Long-polling/WebSocket service broadcasts chunk update notifications to the user's other connected devices.
conceptual_breakdown: Metadata DB: Sharded PostgreSQL / MySQL storing User, File, Folder, FileVersion, and FileChunkMapping tables.
Block Storage: Amazon S3 storing immutable 4MB chunks named by SHA-256 hash.
Conflict Resolution: If two devices edit offline and sync simultaneously, create a conflict file (`Report (Alice's conflicted copy).docx`).

topics.title: Case Study: Design TinyURL / Bitly (Base62 Encoding & Key Generation Service)
topics.definition: Design a scalable URL shortening service handling 100 million new URLs/month and 10 billion clicks/month with sub-10ms redirect latency and 99.999% availability.
topics.why_we_need_it: The essential fundamental interview problem covering Base62 encoding, unique ID generation without collision, 301 vs 302 HTTP redirects, and cache sizing.
topics.real_world_analogy: A cloakroom coat check ticket: you hand over a giant bulky winter coat (Long URL) and receive a tiny plastic token with number '7aB' (Short URL). When you show '7aB', you instantly get your coat back.
topics.how_it_works:
1. Base62 Encoding: Uses `[a-z, A-Z, 0-9]` (62 characters). A 7-character string provides $62^7 \approx 3.52 \text{ Trillion}$ unique short URLs.
2. Key Generation Service (KGS): Dedicated background worker pre-generates billions of unique random 7-character Base62 keys and stores them in a Redis/DB table (`Used` vs `Unused`). When a user requests a short URL, the server instantly grabs a pre-generated unused key without hashing collisions.
3. HTTP Redirect Code: Returns `301 Moved Permanently` (browser caches redirect, saving server load) OR `302 Found` (browser queries server every time, enabling click analytics tracking).
4. Caching: 80/20 rule: Cache top 20% most clicked URLs in Redis RAM for sub-2ms redirect lookups.

topics.title: Case Study: Design Google Web Crawler & PageRank Pipeline
topics.definition: Design a distributed web crawler capable of crawling billions of web pages per month, respecting `robots.txt` politeness, handling DNS resolution bottlenecks, and detecting duplicate web pages.
topics.why_we_need_it: Tests massive distributed queue architectures (Frontier Queues), Bloom Filter URL deduplication, politeness delay engines, and distributed graph PageRank computation.
topics.real_world_analogy: A massive team of explorers mapping every road and signpost in the world: they start at a town square (Seed URLs), follow every road to new towns, note down the names, and mark visited towns on a giant map so they never walk in circles.
topics.how_it_works:
1. URL Frontier: Priority Queues (ranks importance by PageRank/freshness) + Politeness Queues (maps hostnames to FIFO queues with mandatory 1-second host delay timers).
2. DNS Resolver Cache: Dedicated local DNS cache cluster to avoid millions of external DNS lookups.
3. HTML Fetcher & Parser: Fetches HTML via HTTP/2, extracts links, and parses text.
4. Deduplication Engines: Bloom Filters to check if URL was already crawled; SimHash / MinHash to detect duplicate and mirrored web page text.
5. Storage: Raw web pages saved to S3/Bigtable; document graph fed to MapReduce/Spark for PageRank graph calculations.
